payload.title: Honeymoon Planner vs Travel Agent Compared
payload.excerpt: Honeymoon planner vs travel agent sounds like a choice between two kinds of business. The short answer: compare the service, not the title.
key_takeaways: Whichever title a business uses, compare what it will actually do.
Ask every planner or agent the same questions, and get the answers in writing.
Australian consumer guarantees, supplier terms, insurance timing and insolvency risk apply whichever label you choose.
If the honeymoon follows a destination wedding, ask whether the same business can plan the wedding travel and the honeymoon as one plan.

faq.q: Do we need a travel agent for our honeymoon?
faq.a: That is your choice. Consumer guarantees apply whether you book directly or through an agent or intermediary. The choice rests on how much planning you want to hand over and how many moving parts the trip has.

faq.q: Can one business plan both our wedding travel and our honeymoon?
faq.a: Ask directly: whether the same person plans both, and how dates and flights are checked between the two. Get the answer in writing, alongside the fee.

faq.q: Are our rights different if we book through an agent?
faq.a: Consumer guarantees still apply whether you book with the provider, an agent or a booking platform. What changes is the paperwork: the agent's terms and the provider's terms both apply.
Start with two questions: who will we deal with from first call to return, and what will you confirm in writing before we commit?
